question: A developer is deciding how to structure cache_control breakpoints and TTLs across a Messages API request. Select the statements below that are accurate.
options: A) Cache reads are billed at the full base input token rate, identical to a cache miss, so caching never reduces token cost and only saves latency even with custom TTLs.
B) The default ephemeral cache lifetime is 5 minutes; a ttl of "1h" extends this to 1 hour with the write cost approximately twice the base input token write price.
C) Automatic caching, enabled via a single top-level cache_control flag, moves the cache breakpoint forward as a conversation grows without manual per-block placement.
D) Every model supports the same 512-token minimum cacheable prompt length, so cache eligibility never varies by model, ensuring uniform breakpoint behavior across models.
E) Within a single request, up to four explicit cache_control breakpoints can be placed directly on individual content blocks, allowing per-block cache lifetimes.
correct_answers: B) The default ephemeral cache lifetime is 5 minutes; a ttl of "1h" extends this to 1 hour with the write cost approximately twice the base input token write price.
C) Automatic caching, enabled via a single top-level cache_control flag, moves the cache breakpoint forward as a conversation grows without manual per-block placement.
E) Within a single request, up to four explicit cache_control breakpoints can be placed directly on individual content blocks, allowing per-block cache lifetimes.
explanations: Incorrect. Cache reads are billed at a fraction of the base input token rate (approximately 10%), providing a significant cost reduction compared to a cache miss. Therefore, caching reduces token cost as well as latency, even with custom TTLs.

Correct. The default cache lifetime is 5 minutes, and specifying a ttl of "1h" extends it to 1 hour. The write cost for the 1-hour TTL is approximately double the base input token price, compared to 1.25x for the standard 5-minute TTL.

Correct. Automatic caching can be enabled with a single top-level cache_control flag, which simplifies prompt caching. The system then automatically advances the cache breakpoint as the conversation history grows, removing the need for manual per-block breakpoint placement.

Incorrect. The minimum prompt length required for caching varies by model; for example, some models require at least 512 tokens, while others may require up to 4,096 tokens. Thus, cache eligibility is not uniform and breakpoint behavior can differ across models.
Correct. You can place explicit cache_control breakpoints directly on individual content blocks, up to a limit of four per request, and each block can define its own cache lifetime via a TTL.
